events.title: The Eclipse That Stopped a War
events.description: A solar eclipse, famously predicted by the Greek thinker Thales of Miletus, darkened the sky during a battle between the armies of Lydia and Media. Alarmed by the sudden darkness, both sides agreed to a truce.
events.significance: Astronomers and historians treat this eclipse as a fixed reference point for dating other ancient events. It is also an early landmark in scientific prediction.

events.title: Indian Removal Act Signed
events.description: President Andrew Jackson signed the Indian Removal Act. It authorized the federal government to relocate Native American nations from their homelands in the southeastern United States to lands west of the Mississippi River.
events.significance: The law led to forced relocations such as the Trail of Tears. It remains one of the most controversial episodes in American history.

events.title: John Muir Founds the Sierra Club
events.description: In San Francisco, the naturalist John Muir and a group of supporters organized the Sierra Club. Muir became its first president.
events.significance: The club grew into one of the most influential conservation organizations in the United States. It helped shape the movement to protect wilderness and national parks.

events.title: Golden Gate Bridge Opens to Traffic
events.description: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco officially opened to vehicles. President Franklin D. Roosevelt signaled the start of traffic by pushing a button in Washington, DC.
events.significance: The bridge was the longest suspension bridge in the world at the time. It became an enduring symbol of San Francisco and American engineering.

events.title: Palestine Liberation Organization Formed
events.description: The Palestine Liberation Organization was founded. It brought together Palestinian groups seeking national representation.
events.significance: The PLO became a central party in Israeli–Palestinian affairs. Yasser Arafat led it from 1969.
